quotes.name: Ximena Mehta
quotes.quote: Yeah, I still see it that way. Six weeks of mild weather like this — that's not a punishment, that's a gift, and people treat it like one. They walk, they bike, they take the long way home around the lake. I don't look at a quiet 12th Street on a Saturday and think we're losing riders. I look at it and think everyone's outside enjoying the day before the fog rolls back in. That's just Oakland in the spring.

interviews.raw: {"answer":"I wrote that line because I was tired of watching us pat ourselves on the back for a bench while the health center sat unfunded. But six cycles of this weather — you see it in the park, you see it at the library, you see it in the way people linger instead of rushing — and I've got to be honest with you: mild has its own kind of strength. It's the weather that lets a neighbor actually stop and talk. It's the weather that gets kids to stay for the tutoring program. It's not weakness. It's the city catching its breath.
